intro.baseline: This questionnaire measures your current understanding of coaching supervision, supervision skills, ethical awareness, and leadership application. Respond based on how you feel now. There are no right or wrong answers.
intro.debrief: You completed this questionnaire at the start of the module. Answer again based on how you behave now. Then reflect on the module.

subscales.name: Supervision Awareness
subscales.help: These items assess your understanding of what coaching supervision is, how it differs from related practices, and why it matters.

items.text: I understand how coaching supervision differs from mentoring, management oversight, and therapy.
I can identify the three core functions of coaching supervision (normative, formative, restorative).
I recognize that my own emotional reactions during coaching sessions contain valuable information about the coaching relationship.
I am aware of how dynamics in one professional relationship can mirror dynamics in another (parallel process).
Coaching supervision seems unnecessary for experienced coaches who are already effective.

subscales.name: Supervision Skills
subscales.help: These items assess your ability to use supervision-related skills in professional conversations.

items.text: I can examine a coaching case from multiple perspectives, not just the client's presenting issue.
I am able to shift between focusing on content (what happened) and process (what is happening between people) in a reflective conversation.
I can ask reflective questions that help another person develop their own insight rather than providing answers.
I can balance offering support with providing appropriate challenge in a developmental conversation.
I can identify when my own assumptions or emotional reactions may be influencing a coaching or leadership interaction.

subscales.name: Supervision as Ethical & Professional Practice
subscales.help: These items assess your understanding of supervision's role in ethical coaching practice.

items.text: I understand how coaching supervision contributes to ethical decision-making in professional practice.
I recognize that even well-intentioned coaching can produce negative effects for clients without adequate reflection.
A good coach can rely on their intuition and experience without needing external supervision.
I see coaching supervision as a professional responsibility, not just a development opportunity.
I can articulate why professional coaching bodies require or recommend supervision for credentialed coaches.

subscales.name: Leadership Application
subscales.help: These items assess how you apply supervision-related principles in your leadership practice.

items.text: I create structured opportunities for my team to reflect on their professional practice.
I adjust my leadership approach based on what I learn through reflective conversations.
I use the concept of 'multiple lenses' (examining situations from several perspectives) in my leadership decision-making.
I recognize when parallel dynamics are at play, where patterns in one relationship mirror patterns in another.
I model openness to feedback and willingness to examine my own blind spots as a leader.
This module changed my understanding of coaching supervision.
The observation scenario helped me understand what effective supervision feels like from the supervisee's perspective.
The AI simulation gave me practical experience I could not have gained from reading alone.
I feel more prepared to engage in or facilitate coaching supervision conversations after this experience.
The combination of content, observation, and simulation created a more complete learning experience than any single method would have.

open_ended.prompt: What was the most significant insight you gained from this training plan about coaching supervision? How might it change your leadership practice?
Describe a moment during the observation or simulation that surprised you or challenged your assumptions.
How has your understanding of reflective practice and the role of supervision evolved through this experience?
